summary: The requested generic KVPress serving integration is absent from the prepared base. The prior serving candidate cannot be ported safely because it stores independently selected per-layer token sets behind one request-level req_to_token mapping; an adversarial GPU reference demonstrates incorrect attention when layer selections differ. A correct implementation requires a layer/head-aware cache indexing and lifecycle contract across allocation, attention backends, prefix caching, and transfer paths. No partial press utility or unrelated sparse-attention change is presented as the complete feature.

tests.what_was_measured: On the assigned MI350X, independently computed dense attention for layer 0's selected tokens differs from attention obtained through the final layer's shared slot map by max_abs_error=9.597820281982422, reproducing the prior candidate's mapping correctness failure.

tests.what_was_measured: Pinned Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2 sees one AMD Instinct MI350X; ServerArgs exposes no KVPress attributes and importing kvpress raises ModuleNotFoundError.
The adversarial shared-map incompatibility remains reproducible under pytest on the assigned GPU.

remaining_limitations: No one-node KVPress inference path was implemented or claimed.
No generic BasePress compatibility or external kvpress dependency was added.
Llama, Mistral, Phi, Qwen 2/3, and Gemma 3 semantic accuracy remains unverified.
Radix/prompt caching, chunked prefill, CUDA graphs, speculative decoding, sliding-window/hybrid models, quantized KV caches, and prefix sharing remain unsupported for this proposal.
Tensor, pipeline, and data parallelism remain unverified.
PD disaggregation and KV transfer backends remain unverified.
No native source changed, so a native rebuild was not applicable.
